question_text: A block of mass 10 kg rests on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of friction is 0.3, what is the frictional force when a force of 20 N is applied? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Max friction = μmg = 0.3×100 = 30 N; Since 20 N < 30 N, friction = 20 N

question_text: The limiting frictional force between two surfaces depends on:
explanation: Friction depends on nature of surfaces and normal reaction only.

question_text: A body of mass 5 kg slides down a plane inclined at 30°. If the coefficient of friction is 0.2, what is the frictional force? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Normal reaction = mgcos30° = 5×10×0.866 = 43.3 N; Friction = μR = 0.2×43.3 = 8.66 N

An inclined plane of length 10 m is used to raise a load of 200 N to a height of 2 m. What is the effort required if the machine is 100% efficient?
explanation: VR = l/h = 10/2 = 5; MA = VR = 5; Effort = Load/MA = 200/5 = 40 N
